author: Nayan Seth
description:
Former Anthropic and OpenAI researcher Jacob Coxon said he was 90 per cent certain that China already had spies inside both US artificial intelligence (AI) companies, without providing evidence.
Coxon made the allegation in an interview with entrepreneur Patrick Bet-David on the PBD Podcast, arguing that China could steal advances from leading US AI labs and quickly close any technological gap.
“Right now, if we just stopped, they would try and catch up. But I think one really important thing...
title: ‘China already has spies’ at US AI labs, former Anthropic researcher warns

author: Dewey Sim
description:
US President Donald Trump pressed his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping to roll back China’s export curbs on Japan during their meeting in the US, urging talks between the Chinese and Japanese leaders as Tokyo seeks to manage mounting pressure from Beijing.
People familiar with the discussions told the South China Morning Post that Xi also warned Trump about the growing risks of Japanese militarism during their sit-down in Washington last month.
According to the people, while the issue was not one...
title: Trump urged Xi to talk to Takaichi and lift export curbs on Japan, sources say

author: Teresa Elena Frontado
description:
The US Treasury on Wednesday announced its first penalty under rules governing American investment in sensitive Chinese technologies, revealing a US$200,000 fine against the parent of Plug and Play Tech Centre for failing to report an investment in a Shanghai robotics AI company.
The Treasury said on Wednesday that Amidi, LLC failed to submit a required notification after its Chinese fund subsidiary invested around US$92,478 in Shanghai Qiongche Intelligent Technology Company Limited, known as...
title: US issues first outbound investment fine over Chinese robotics AI deal

author: Teresa Elena Frontado
description:
The United States has proposed requiring universities and other certified schools to pay US$70,000 for each foreign student entering a post-graduation work programme, a measure that could sharply raise the cost for thousands of Chinese graduates seeking employment experience in the country.
The Department of Homeland Security announced on Wednesday that the proposed fee would apply to initial participation in Optional Practical Training, or OPT, with a further US$30,000 charge for subsequent...
title: US proposes US$70,000 fee for foreign students to work after graduation

author: Ling Xin
description:
Initial results from the world’s first two working nuclear clocks indicate that China’s timepiece is about six times as stable as the one in Vienna, according to papers published this week by the journal Nature.
The clocks were developed independently but both the Chinese team, led by Tsinghua University in Beijing, and the researchers at Vienna’s TU Wien used thorium-229 nuclei embedded in crystals to keep time by the steady rhythm of the atom’s core, rather than the electrons whirling around...
title: China’s thorium-229 nuclear clock beats Vienna’s on stability, studies show

author: Shi Huang
description:
“Science has no borders,” Arup Neogi, an India-born scientist who works at a US-sanctioned university, told Chinese state media.
Neogi’s speciality is photonics, the study of generating, controlling and detecting light. At the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China (UESTC) in the southwestern city of Chengdu, he leads a team exploring the interconnection between light and sound.
This university has one of China’s top electronics and communication programmes and has been on the...
title: India-born US citizen drives research into light at sanctioned Chinese school

author: Mustafa Bilal
description:
In December 2022, a Chinese J-11 fighter came within metres of a US RC-135 surveillance plane over the South China Sea, according to the US military, which criticised it as an unsafe manoeuvre. China, however, held the American crew responsible and claimed the RC-135 had suddenly veered towards the Chinese jet despite repeated warnings. Both sides released video footage, yet neither accepted the other’s account of the incident.
This and other such close encounters involved human pilots. The next...
title: US and China must set rules before autonomous fighters cross paths

author: Finbarr Bermingham
description:
The European Parliament voted for a significantly tougher China position on Wednesday, despite strong and long-standing lobbying from Beijing to tone down its official stance.
The chamber backed stronger actions against Beijing, stating it is a “decisive enabler” of Russia, calling for a “continuous [European] naval presence and joint exercises” in and around the Taiwan Strait, and urging swift action to counter Beijing’s industrial policy, which it described as an “existential threat to the...
title: ‘No more dumping, no more spying’: European Parliament hardens line on China

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
The Philippine Coast Guard will receive three longer-range aircraft from the US, two of them modified for improved surveillance, giving Manila greater reach and endurance to monitor Chinese coastguard, naval and research vessels across the South China Sea.
Under a US$39.6 million contract awarded by the United States Navy on September 28, the three second-hand, extended-range King Air 350-series aircraft will be fitted with extended-range fuel systems, upgraded Garmin avionics and high-frequency...
title: How will new longer-range aircraft boost Manila’s South China Sea surveillance?

author: Fan Chen
description:
China and the US – Iran’s key partner and its chief adversary – found firmer common ground on Tehran at the Washington summit last month, and further head-of-state diplomacy could work in Iran’s favour, according to analysts.
Iran was on the agenda when the presidents of the United States and China met in Beijing in May and again in Washington in September.
There was no direct reference to Tehran in Beijing’s statement after the May summit, but following the September meeting China was more...
title: How closer China-US ties – and more Xi-Trump summits – could work in Iran’s favour

author: SCMP
description:
We have put together stories from our coverage on science from the past two weeks to help you stay informed. If you would like to see more of our reporting, please consider subscribing.
1. Chinese researchers say missile lidar model can spot US F-35 at up to 61.5km
A computer simulation developed by Chinese researchers suggests that a missile-borne system with the latest light detection and ranging system, or lidar, could detect and track an F-35 stealth fighter at up to 61.5km (38 miles) at...
title: China’s missile lidar model; world’s most accurate atomic clock: 7 science highlights

author: Finbarr Bermingham
description:
The European Union’s top trade mandarins depart for Beijing on Wednesday for two days of intensive negotiations but expectations in Brussels are measured as to what the talks will deliver.
Maros Sefcovic, the EU’s trade chief, will meet his Chinese counterpart Wang Wentao on Thursday and Friday – three months after their last encounter in Brussels, when the Europeans set an October deadline for signs of a rebalancing in the trading relationship.
Non-stop working-level talks have proven...
title: Last chance saloon: EU presses China for a sign to prove trade talks can work

author: Dannie Peng
description:
Climate change and agricultural development have brought a new goose population to China with unique migratory patterns, a study has found.
In an article on the Chinese Academy of Sciences website, researchers from the CAS Institute of Zoology said they had discovered a “genetically distinct” population of swan geese that emerged in Beijing over the past century.
They said the timing of their arrival coincided with environmental shifts in the region during the early 20th century – namely climate...
title: Climate change and farming gave rise to ‘genetically distinct’ Beijing swan goose: study

author: Caroline Lin
description:
Creators of China’s first Tibetan-language AI model have pledged to speed up upgrades aimed at promoting ethnic integration.
Approaches to advancing the large language model, DeepZang, were discussed at a seminar on Monday that brought together representatives from research institutes, universities and enterprises, according to state-run portal Chinanews.com.
It said the event held in Hohhot, in China’s northern Inner Mongolia autonomous region, addressed issues such as improving Tibetan...
title: China’s DeepZang AI aims to transform Tibetan language tech, promote ethnic unity
